event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, dated February 16 2022, repeatedly links AT&T’s current and future performance to the COVID-19 pandemic, a recent global crisis well within the ≤3-year ‘recent event’ window, so elevated risk scores (up to 10) are permissible under the Time Decay Principle.  The disclosure spans both realized impacts (e.g., lost advertising revenue, higher production costs, store closures, supply-chain delays) and forward-looking uncertainties (e.g., customer payment risk, roaming-revenue pressure, labour shortages, bandwidth-driven cap-ex).  Language is largely specific—naming affected business units (WarnerMedia, Business Wireline, Retail, Call-centres), describing cost drivers (hybrid film distribution, safety protocols), and identifying revenue lines (sports advertising, roaming, suppliers).  Quantification is qualitative rather than numeric, but repeated use of “material,” “significant,” and “higher costs” signals meaningful magnitude.  Mitigating language (“may,” “could”) is present, but seldom paired with concrete remedies, so overall severity remains high.  Because the pandemic’s operational and financial effects are ongoing and multifaceted, and the statements include both experienced hits and credible future threats, I judge the overall COVID-19 risk level for AT&T as ‘high.’  Individual sentences that cite direct, already-incurred impacts or specify vulnerable revenue streams earn the highest micro-scores (8–9); generic or heavily qualified statements score lower (3–5).

No quantified magnitude.

evidence_list.snippet: At the onset in 2020, mitigation measures caused sports leagues to modify their seasons and suspend certain operations, which adversely affected our advertising revenues and, resulted in contract disputes concerning carriage rights that caused us to incur expenses relating to certain of these sporting events notwithstanding their cancellation.
